proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 803, USA (Unpaved Surface Area) is specifically described in the IRR as what type of open space?

options.text: The 'permitted open space' — any outdoor area not covered by the building structure including driveways and paved courts
The 'true open space' — the portion that must remain unpaved with exposed soil and planting for ecological function
The 'required open space' — the minimum front setback distance mandated by the local zoning ordinance
The 'total open space' — all lot area not occupied by the enclosed building footprint including paved open areas

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 803.3.b.ii explicitly describes USA as the 'true open space' — the portion of TLA that must remain unpaved with exposed soil and planting. It serves stormwater percolation, microclimate cooling, and groundwater recharge. Option A describes ISA (driveways, paved courts). Option C describes setback requirements, not USA. Option D describes TOSL (= ISA + USA), not USA alone.
proposed.explanation: USA = 'true open space' per the IRR. TOSL = ISA + USA = all non-building open space (hard + soft). USA is the soft/permeable portion only. The distinction matters: a developer cannot satisfy the USA minimum with concrete pavers — it must be actual unpaved soil and planting.
